items.headline: Man jailed 16 weeks for abandoning 71 cats in a Bukit Panjang flat
items.summary: Muhammad Khairul Naim Zainol, 37, was sentenced on 23 September after leaving 71 cats without power or water for nearly two years, causing nine deaths. He pleaded guilty to 24 charges under the Animals and Birds Act and was barred from owning pets for 12 months.

items.headline: DPM Gan urges Singapore and China to deepen AI and green-economy ties
items.summary: At the FutureChina Global Forum on 25 September, Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Gan Kim Yong said the Singapore-China relationship has “never been static” and called for a next phase of cooperation in AI and the green economy, building on the Suzhou Industrial Park.

items.headline: Activist charged over candlelight vigils for two executed drug traffickers
items.summary: S Suraendher Kumarr, 32, was charged on 25 September with three Public Order Act offences over unpermitted candlelight assemblies near Changi Prison and a gathering at the State Courts calling for abolition of the death penalty. He was granted S$5,000 bail.

items.headline: Driver, 62, jailed 13 months for running a red light and dragging a pregnant woman
items.summary: Chen Zhiguang was sentenced on 24 September to 13 months’ jail and a 10-year driving ban after running a red light on Upper Changi Road East in July 2025, hitting a woman who was 15 weeks pregnant. She was hospitalised for 59 days with multiple fractures.

items.headline: Coroner’s inquiry opens into cabby killed by his own moving taxi
items.summary: An inquiry opened on 24 September into the death of taxi driver Tee Chin Teong, 66, who died in February 2025 along Jalan Besar after his taxi rolled forward as he helped passengers with luggage, trapping him against a parked lorry.

items.headline: Tata Sons defies majority owner Tata Trusts as control feud heads to court
items.summary: Tata Sons’ board reappointed chairman N. Chandrasekaran in a 4-1 vote and moved toward a possible IPO, but Tata Trusts, which owns a majority stake, declared the move void, setting up a court battle over control of the $18-billion-plus group.

items.headline: India fast-tracks Canada and Mexico trade talks amid US tariff pressure
items.summary: India is accelerating free-trade negotiations with Canada and Mexico, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney citing “good progress” and Prime Minister Narendra Modi expected to visit Canada around the December G20 summit.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today’s edition
items.summary: BBC and Sky News, and the fallback outlets The Guardian, CNN, Bloomberg and Al Jazeera, returned no verifiable UK-domestic story within the 48-hour window that could be sourced from this edition’s network environment. No item was fabricated to fill the gap.

items.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts six Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said on 24 September that air defences shot down six ballistic missiles targeting the Red Sea port of Yanbu and the city of Taif, blaming Iran-aligned Houthis, who claimed a wider barrage on Jazan and Aramco facilities.

items.headline: Pakistan PM Sharif tells UN a Houthi attack on Mecca or Medina is a ‘red line’
items.summary: In his UN General Assembly address on 25 September, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, warning that any threat to Mecca and Medina must never be crossed, and renewed calls for a UN-backed Kashmir plebiscite.

items.headline: Russia’s ruling party secures 349 of 450 Duma seats as final results confirmed
items.summary: Final results from Russia’s State Duma election gave United Russia about 57.8% of the list vote and 349 of 450 seats, up from 2021. Notably, 46 war veterans, 41 of them from United Russia, won seats in the new parliament.

items.headline: Iraq’s prime minister calls for a sovereign Palestinian state at the UN
items.summary: Addressing the UN General Assembly on 25 September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi called for the establishment of a sovereign state of Palestine, joining a wave of leaders pressing the statehood question during the high-level week.

items.headline: Anthropic says its Claude AI autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system
items.summary: Anthropic’s new life-sciences lab said Claude uncovered a previously uncharacterised enzyme system in bacteriophage DNA during a roughly 21.5-hour autonomous run spanning 949 sessions and 215.6 million tokens, scanning about 200,000 enzymes. Its function is not yet understood.

items.headline: Meta puts its Muse AI agent into Ray-Ban glasses at Connect 2026
items.summary: At Meta Connect on 23 September, Meta brought its Muse personal AI agent to its smart glasses and showed a real-time video avatar, alongside new Ray-Ban Meta hardware and a $1,299 VR headset due in spring 2027.

items.headline: AI-infrastructure startups Modal and Baseten in fresh funding talks
items.summary: Bloomberg reported on 23 September that Modal and Baseten, which help businesses run AI models on Nvidia GPUs and standard chips, are in talks to raise new funding, underscoring investor demand for the tools that serve AI inference workloads.

items.headline: Anthropic signs a $11.6bn, seven-year computing deal with Akamai
items.summary: Anthropic agreed a seven-year, $11.6 billion contract, expandable to $20 billion, for Akamai CPU capacity, plus a warrant to buy about 5% of Akamai at $111.33 a share. Akamai shares jumped as much as 16.4% to $128.46 on 25 September.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds Friday as the Dow jumps 478 points to cap a winning week
items.summary: The Dow rose 478.64 points, or 0.93%, to 51,828.62 on 25 September, while the S&P 500 added 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq gained 0.5% to 27,068.72, as easing oil prices and calmer Treasury markets drove a rebound. For the week the Nasdaq rose 2%.

items.headline: Costco caps fiscal 2026 with a Q4 beat as net sales rise 11.2% to $93.9bn
items.summary: For the 16 weeks to 30 August, Costco reported net sales up 11.2% to $93.9 billion and adjusted earnings of $6.60 a share, beating the $6.53 consensus. Comparable sales rose 9.4% and the retailer plans 28 net new warehouses in fiscal 2027.

items.headline: MGM Resorts shares sink 11% as Barry Diller’s People drops an $18bn buyout
items.summary: People Inc., which owns a 26.1% stake, withdrew its June offer of $48.30 a share, valuing MGM Resorts at about $18 billion, citing difficulty raising equity. MGM shares fell 11% and the casino operator will remain a standalone company.

items.headline: US jobless claims slip to 197,000, near a 57-year low
items.summary: Initial claims fell 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended 19 September, below the 201,000 poll estimate and the lowest since mid-July, while the four-week average dropped to 202,250, signalling continued labour-market resilience.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell takes Baku pole as points leader Antonelli crashes out in Q1
items.summary: George Russell claimed pole for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix ahead of Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start 16th after hitting a wall in Q1. Isack Hadjar out-qualified Max Verstappen on his return from injury; the race runs Saturday.

items.headline: 🎾 Shapovalov earns his 250th tour win as Mannarino downs former champ Shang in Chengdu
items.summary: Denis Shapovalov recorded the 250th tour-level win of his career at the Chengdu Open, while Adrian Mannarino knocked out former champion Shang Juncheng, as the ATP 250 reached its later rounds on 24 September.

items.headline: 🏏 Nepal upset Afghanistan by five wickets in the Asian Games men’s cricket
items.summary: Spinners Kushal Bhurtel and Lalit Rajbanshi shared seven wickets as Nepal bowled Afghanistan out for 102 for 7 and chased 103 for 5 with 16 balls to spare on 25 September, opening their Asian Games campaign with a win in Nisshin.

items.headline: 🏏 Hong Kong beat Oman by 41 runs as Ayush Shukla takes 3 for 13
items.summary: Hong Kong posted 121 for 8 and restricted Oman to 80 for 6 to win by 41 runs in Nisshin on 25 September, with Ayush Shukla claiming 3 for 13, lifting Hong Kong to second in Group A of the Asian Games men’s cricket.

items.headline: Croatia becomes the 74th nation to sign NASA’s Artemis Accords
items.summary: Croatia signed the Artemis Accords on 23 September at a ceremony in Zagreb, becoming the 74th signatory to the US-led framework for peaceful space exploration. Science minister Radovan Fuchs signed on the country’s behalf, days after Albania became the 73rd.

items.headline: Exotic ‘non-Abelian anyons’ achieve the full toolkit for universal quantum computing
items.summary: Researchers from UChicago, Harvard, Stony Brook and Quantinuum used 54 qubits on the H2 processor to combine braiding and fusion of non-Abelian anyons, unlocking the full set of operations for universal quantum computing. The work was published in Nature.

items.headline: Astronomers confirm Elias 2-24 b as the youngest known planet
items.summary: A Jupiter-sized world orbiting a star about 450 light-years away, Elias 2-24 b is less than one million years old, smashing the previous record of roughly five million years. Its rapid formation challenges leading theories of how giant planets assemble.

items.headline: JWST’s mysterious ‘little red dots’ explained as young supermassive black holes
items.summary: A Nature study argues the enigmatic ‘little red dots’ seen by the James Webb Space Telescope are young supermassive black holes wrapped in dense cocoons of ionised gas, implying black-hole masses far lower than earlier estimates.

fun_fact.headline: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt
fun_fact.body: The country with the most pyramids is not Egypt — it is Sudan. The ancient Kingdom of Kush built well over 200 pyramids along the Nile at sites such as Meroë, more than twice the number in Egypt. Sudan’s pyramids are far smaller and steeper than their Egyptian cousins, and most remain little visited today.
fun_fact.source: National Geographic; Sky HISTORY; Wikipedia (Pyramids of Meroë)

puzzle.title: Ahead of His Time
puzzle.body: A wealthy collector proudly displays a framed photograph said to show the composer Ludwig van Beethoven seated at his piano. A visiting historian glances at it for barely a second and declares it a fake — with no chemical test, and knowing nothing unusual about Beethoven’s appearance. How can she be so certain?
puzzle.approach: Don’t hunt for a flaw in the picture itself — ask what it claims to be, and whether that was even possible.
puzzle.answer: Beethoven died in 1827. The earliest photographs of people were not made until about 1838–1839, when Louis Daguerre’s process first captured human subjects. So no genuine photograph of Beethoven can exist — he died more than a decade before photography could record a living person. Any ‘photo’ of him must be a fake or, at best, a photograph of a painting.

word_puzzle.title: Letters Don’t Lie
word_puzzle.body:
Each phrase below uses exactly the same letters as its answer — and hints at it. Unscramble all five:

1. DIRTY ROOM   (9)
2. THEY SEE   (3, 4)
3. CASH LOST IN ME   (4, 8)
4. HERE COME DOTS   (3, 5, 4)
5. ELEVEN PLUS TWO   (6, 4, 3)
word_puzzle.approach: Each clue is an anagram whose scrambled words slyly describe the answer. Rearrange all the letters into a single word or phrase.
word_puzzle.answer:
1. DIRTY ROOM → DORMITORY
2. THEY SEE → THE EYES
3. CASH LOST IN ME → SLOT MACHINES
4. HERE COME DOTS → THE MORSE CODE
5. ELEVEN PLUS TWO → TWELVE PLUS ONE

Each one is self-describing: the letters of the clue rearrange into the very thing it names.
